review_candidates.title: SVP - Chief Financial Officer, Latin America
review_candidates.description: Job Description TTI Professional (Milwaukee Tool) & Consumer (Ryobi) Businesses At TTI, our people and culture are the foundation of our success. We are committed to developing leaders who drive innovation, move with speed and urgency, challenge the status quo, and build high-performing teams capable of delivering exceptional results. The Chief Financial Officer, Latin America is the senior-most finance executive for the region, accountable for the financial strategy, performance, governance, capital allocation, risk management, and long-term value creation of Milwaukee Tool’s professional business and Ryobi’s consumer business throughout Latin America. This leader serves as a strategic partner to the regional business president, global finance leadership, and TTI executive leadership, providing the financial judgment, discipline, and enterprise perspective needed to accelerate profitable growth, scale the organization, and steward the region’s financial health. This role is ideal for a commercially minded CFO who can operate as both strategist and steward, shaping business strategy, testing investment choices, protecting financial integrity, and building the finance infrastructure required to support a complex, fast-growing, multi-country business. Your Responsibilities Own Financial Strategy, Performance, and Value Creation Serve as the senior financial steward for Latin America, accountable for regional financial strategy, business performance, capital discipline, and long-term value creation. Own the region’s financial outcomes, including revenue growth, profitability, margin expansion, cash flow, working capital, capital efficiency, and return on invested capital. Lead long-range financial planning, annual operating planning, forecasting, performance management, scenario modeling, and monthly business reviews that translate strategy into measurable financial plans. Advise regional and corporate leadership on capital allocation, investment prioritization, pricing strategy, market expansion, cost structure, and resource tradeoffs. Ensure regional financial commitments are delivered while balancing near-term performance with sustainable growth, enterprise risk, and shareholder value creation. Serve as Strategic CFO and Executive Business Partner Operate as a trusted advisor to the regional president, global finance leadership, and TTI executive leadership on the financial implications of business strategy, growth priorities, and major operating decisions. Bring an enterprise perspective to decision-making by connecting financial performance, commercial strategy, operational execution, risk, talent, and organizational capability. Partner with commercial, product, marketing, operations, and supply chain leaders to evaluate strategic investments, pricing and margin opportunities, channel strategy, product launches, M&A opportunities, and market expansion initiatives. Provide executive-level financial narratives, insights, and recommendations for regional and corporate operating reviews, strategic planning discussions, investment decisions, and governance forums. Identify material risks, opportunities, and performance gaps early; recommend clear actions to protect the business, improve returns, and accelerate growth. Build a Scalable, High-Performing Finance Organization Recruit, develop, and retain a world-class finance organization across multiple countries. Create strong succession plans and leadership development pipelines. Develop financial acumen throughout the organization and act as a coach to business leaders. Build scalable systems, processes, and structures that support future growth. Foster collaboration across regional and global teams while reinforcing a One-Team mentality. Lead Governance, Risk, Controls, Tax, Treasury, and Financial Integrity Own the region’s accounting, controllership, financial reporting, tax, treasury, audit, compliance, and internal control environment across multiple countries and currencies. Ensure financial integrity, policy adherence, statutory compliance, corporate governance, and strong stewardship of company assets across all Latin America operations. Manage regional liquidity, cash flow, foreign exchange exposure, working capital, tax planning, and capital structure considerations in partnership with corporate finance and treasury. Lead audit readiness, risk mitigation, control remediation, and governance improvements that strengthen transparency, accountability, and confidence in regional financial results. Drive simplification, automation, standardization, and analytics capabilities that improve speed, accuracy, decision support, and the scalability of the finance function. Lead Growth, Transformation, and Strategic Change Provide CFO leadership for new market expansion, acquisitions, integration activity, business model evolution, and organizational scaling across Latin America. Lead cross-functional initiatives requiring financial strategy, business case development, governance, stakeholder alignment, and disciplined execution across countries and functions. Champion adoption of systems, tools, dashboards, and operating rhythms that increase financial visibility, improve forecast accuracy, and enable faster executive decision-making. Model a culture of ownership, constructive challenge, financial discipline, transparency, and relentless improvement. The successful candidate will demonstrate TTI’s leadership expectations and cultural competencies: Drives Growth & Innovation Thinks strategically while maintaining strong operational execution. Identifies new opportunities to accelerate profitable growth. Challenges conventional thinking and drives innovative solutions. Drives Execution Delivers commitments with speed, urgency, and accountability. Establishes clear priorities and aligns resources to maximize impact. Balances short-term results with long-term business objectives. Builds Collaborative Relationships Creates trust across functions, geographies, and leadership levels. Influences without authority and successfully navigates complex organizations. Communicates candidly, directly, and constructively. Builds Organizational Capacity Recruits and develops exceptional talent. Provides frequent, actionable coaching and feedback. Creates an engaged, high-performing culture that scales with business growth. Fosters transparency and encourages issue escalation and problem solving. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or related field required. MBA and/or CPA preferred. Executive presence and credibility to influence senior leaders, challenge assumptions, communicate complex financial issues clearly, and represent the region in corporate governance and strategic planning forums. 15+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, including experience as a CFO, divisional CFO, regional CFO, or senior finance executive for a complex, multi-country business. Demonstrated success leading financial strategy, capital allocation, enterprise planning, performance management, treasury, tax, controls, compliance, and governance in an international environment. Strong commercial orientation with experience partnering directly with presidents, general managers, corporate CFOs, and executive leadership teams to shape business strategy and improve financial returns. Experience operating in high-growth, matrixed, multi-currency environments with the ability to balance speed, control, local complexity, and enterprise standards. Deep understanding of accounting, internal controls, audit, tax, treasury, regulatory requirements, and compliance expectations across Latin America. Proven ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing finance teams with succession depth, business partnership capability, and strong controllership discipline. Fluent English required; Spanish and/or Portuguese strongly preferred. Location in LA region and/or South Florida Milwaukee Tool is an equal opportunity employer.

review_candidates.title: Regulatory Affairs Manager APAC (m/f/d), Regulatory Affairs ROW
review_candidates.description: Merz Aesthetics is an independent, internationally active company in the field of aesthetic medicine. For years, our comprehensive product portfolio is among the highest quality in its category and is valued by healthcare professionals worldwide. Merz Aesthetics is part of the Merz Group, with our Europe , Middle East and Africa (EMEA) headquarters in Frankfurt am Main. Our global head office is located in Raleigh, North Carolina, USA. Our purpose is to help people look better, feel better, and live better, and over 3,000 employees across 26 countries are dedicated to this mission. Would you like to become part of our success story? Join Merz Aesthetics! The Following Responsibilities Are Awaiting You You prepare and submit applications for new marketing authorizations / registrations and respond to questions in a timely and accurate manner. You compile and update high-quality dossiers for marketing authorizations / registrations. You advise concerned development departments regarding the quality, analytical methods, pre-clinical and clinical development to ensure acceptance of the data worldwide. You maintain and manage the lifecycle of products worldwide, including the preparation and submission of applications for renewals, variations, submissions, and annual reports in due time. You coordinate change control procedures, including the collection of regulatory assessments worldwide and their international implementation. You coordinate regulatory projects and communicate with third parties concerning regulatory issues. You coordinate the development of regulatory strategies and participate in project teams. You evaluate (new) IT tools to support and facilitate product registration and maintenance as well as maintain the regulatory databases to ensure they are correct and up to date. You conduct due diligence for established products with regard to regulatory aspects. You prepare and update product information texts according to company core data and relevant guidelines and manage translations. What We Expect From You You have a natural scientific or medical device engineering background (e.g., pharmacist, biologist, chemist), with approbation, diploma, master’s degree, or PhD. You bring approximately 3–5 years of experience in international Regulatory Affairs within the medical device industry, with a strong focus on high-risk (Class III) medical devices. You have in-depth knowledge of global and APAC medical device regulations and hands-on experience managing regulatory submissions, registrations, renewals, change notifications, and approvals across key APAC markets, including China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, Singapore, and Thailand. You understand regulatory pathways and requirements for medical devices, including energy-based systems, implants, injectables, and combination products. You are experienced in preparing and reviewing technical files and submission dossiers, labeling and IFU reviews, regulatory strategies and gap assessments. You proactively monitor evolving regulatory requirements and standards across APAC, assess the business impact of regulatory changes, and develop effective compliance strategies to support organizational objectives. You have a solid understanding of quality management systems and standards, such as ISO 13485, and ideally bring experience supporting audits, inspections, and interactions with regulatory authorities. You communicate fluently in English, and additional language skills in Chinese and/or Japanese would be a strong advantage. What You Can Expect From Us Putting people first : You can expect to find an open work culture with flat hierarchies and short decision-making paths at Merz Aesthetics.
